Content: Josh Allen celebrates the Bills’ opening weekend victory.Photograph: Tim Warner/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenJosh Allen celebrates the Bills’ opening weekend victory.Photograph: Tim Warner/Getty ImagesBuffalo BillsThe Josh Allen rollercoaster is up and running again for the new NFL seasonThe Bills quarterback produced his usual thrills: a galloping touchdown run, a near game-ending mistake and a brilliant throw. Buffalo fans better hold onDoug FarrarMon 14 Sep 2026 03.30 EDTLast modified on Mon 14 Sep 2026 12.58 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleHaving Josh Allen as your quarterback is a bit like owning a high-performance sports car with an odd mechanical flaw that can’t be repaired. Most of the results are amazing – perhaps unprecedented – but there are also times when you wonder if a safer ride would get you farther.In Buffalo’s 36-31 win over the Houston Texans on Sunday, Bills fans saw all sides of the Allenmobile. The quarterback completed 20 of 29 passes for 334 yards, two touchdowns, no interceptions and a passer rating of 130.5. He also ran the ball six times for 23 yards and twomoretouchdowns, the first a typicalromp through the opposing defense.A two-play sequence perfectly summarized the Allen rollercoaster. There was his desperation heave into the end zone with 1:48 left in the game when the Bills were down 31-30. Texans cornerbackKamari Lassiter droppedwhat should have been an easy game-sealing interception, which gave Allen the second chance he needed to thread the needle onthis amazing 34-yard touchdown passto receiver Joshua Palmer.Allow content provided by a third party?This article includes content hosted onembed.bsky.app. We ask for your permission before anything is loaded, as the provider may be using cookies and other technologies. To view this content,click 'Allow and continue'.Allow and continueThe Texans had one more chance to pull the game out, but CJ Stroud fumbled the ball on a sack with 16 seconds left, and that was that. Stroud, by the way, is playing this season for his secondNFLcontract, which is a strange place for an alleged franchise quarterback to be. Stroud has been up and down in the two full seasons since he was the Offensive Rookie of the Year in 2023, but he did his level best here. This time, Good Josh Allen – and an inability to capitalize on Bad Josh Allen – sank the opponent.JJ Watt proves to be a solid replacement for Tony Romo as CBS’s No 1 analystRead moreIn fairness, Allen has cut down on his devotion to hero ball and become a much safer player in recent seasons. He committed 37 total turnovers in the 2022 and 2023 seasons combined, and just 18 combined in 2024 and 2025. And those errors often came because the Bills’ shortcomings meant he had to take risks. Once again, this game presented a situation in which Allen had to be Superman for his team to win.We’ve seen that all too often before, and Bills fans have hoped that a more balanced team may take Allen to a Super Bowl for the first time.The balance isn’t here yet. New defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard is one of the NFL’s more highly regarded assistant coaches, but the Texans put his defense through it with strong performances from Stroud and running back David Montgomery. For a large part of Sunday, this looked a lot like the Same Old Bills we’ve seen before.Still, both teams showed enough in this game to suggest they will be contenders in the AFC. One thing’s for sure: if they meet again in the postseason, get ready for all kinds of fireworks.View image in fullscreenDerrick Henry shows few signs of slowing down in his 30s.Photograph: Andy Lyons/Getty ImagesMVP of the weekDerrick Henry, RB, Baltimore Ravens.Henry wasn’t the only Ravens offensive player who showed his stuff in Baltimore’s 41-23 win over the Indianapolis Colts. Lamar Jackson was his usual amazing self, andZay Flowers outran Indy’s entire defenseon his 54-yard touchdown catch. But it was Henry, the Ravens’ 32-year-old running back, who set the tone in the win. Henry carried the ball 24 times for 144 yards andthree touchdowns, adding a 19-yard catch for good measure.It was a historic day for Henry, who passed Marcus Allen on the NFL’s all-time rushing touchdowns listwith 125, trailing only Emmitt Smith and LaDainian Tomlinson.Not bad for an older guy.Video of the weekAllow content provided by a third party?This article includes content hosted onembed.bsky.app. We ask for your permission before anything is loaded, as the provider may be using cookies and other technologies. To view this content,click 'Allow and continue'.Allow and continueAfter the Cleveland Browns’ 34-10 embarrassment of a loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars, in whichDeshaun Watson was unforgivably badfor the most part, head coach Todd Monken was asked why he stuck with the quarterback throughout the game. He came up with some excellent word salad.“We’ll analyze everything that we do,”Monken said of Watson. “It’s not just him, OK? We’re putting this on Deshaun, OK, which is unfair. And whatever there is externally doesn’t matter to me. That doesn’t affect me. That has nothing to do with my decision making. … My decision making is what’s best for the Browns now and moving forward.”It’s pretty clear that the decision to go with Watson over Shedeur Sanders, Dillon Gabriel or anybody else on the roster is more the result of the sunk cost fallacy tied toWatson’s impossible contract, and the Browns’ ownership desperately trying to extract something – anything – from the worst trade in football history. And Monken, who inherited this disaster along with his first NFL head coaching job, has to toe the company line. But whoever is making the Watson decision week after week had better wake up and understand how bad the play on the field is before the locker room is lost for good.Stat of the week59.The Chicago Bears are one of the NFL’s foundational franchises. They began their history as the Decatur Staleys in the old American Professional Football Association and became the Chicago Bears when the APFA became the NFL in 1922.So, whenever the Bears make franchise history, it’s a big deal. The Bears did just that in their 59-37 trampling of the Carolina Panthers on Sunday, scoring their most points ever in a season opener, and participating in the highest-scoring season opener in NFL history, eclipsingthe 88 points scoredby the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and New Orleans Saints in 2018.How did these Bears put up all those points? Caleb Williams completed 21 of 29 passes for 269 yards and two touchdowns, and he also scored two rushing touchdowns – two of Chicago’ssixscores on the ground.In August, Bears head coach Ben Johnson said thathe wanted his 2026 team to have the highest-scoring offense ever. At this rate, he may be on to something.Now, about that defense …View image in fullscreenJustin Herbert encountered the same old problems Sunday.Photograph: Chris Torres/EPAElsewhere around the league-- Over the last 10 seasons, nobody has lost more games than the New York Jets.Their 49-116-0 record and .297 win percentagemark the NFL’s nadir, but perhaps the 2026 Jets are capable of rising from the muck. They certainly looked more sporty in their 23-10 win over the Tennessee Titans. Geno Smith completed 19 of 24 passes for 215 yards, Breece Hall led a rushing attack that put up 152 yards and two touchdowns on 39 carries, and while the Jets were unable to generate an interception in this game aftermaking history in 2025 by failing to record a single pick, said defense did appear spicier, limiting Tennessee to 195 net yards. Not that the Titans are on the verge of competitiveness, but these Jets do have a lot of talent on their roster. Perhaps head coach Aaron Glenn is ready to make the most of it.-- The Denver Broncos and the Kansas City Chiefs face off on Monday Night Football for early control of the AFC West, but the Los Angeles Chargers were supposed to at least challenge those two titans this season. The main reason for the Chargers’ confidence was the brilliant mind of new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel. Justin Herbert has never had an offensive coordinator who could unleash his estimable tools, especially in the deep passing game, andthe quarterback’s 65-yard preseason touchdown pass to Quentin Johnstonwas expected to be the first of many big plays in this new offense. It didn’t quite go that way on Sunday in the Chargers’ 26-14 loss to the Arizona Cardinals, who have generally been awful for years. Herbert attempted just two passes of 20 or more air yards,completing one. Overall, he looked the scheme-limited player he has been so far in his Chargers career.-- Are we ready for a Carson Wentz rebirth? The Minnesota Vikings have experienced some awful (albeit self-inflicted) quarterback luck since they let Sam Darnold sign with the Seattle Seahawks in 2025 and named 2024 first-round pick JJ McCarthy the starter. Head coach Kevin O’Connell’s well-deserved reputation as a quarterback whisperer didn’t extend to McCarthy,who looks like a major bust. And the Vikings’ offseason signing of Kyler Murray threw an interception on his first pass against the Green Bay Packers, before suffering a concussion in the first quarter.Murray was replaced by Wentz, who went from franchise QB to multi-team journeyman in his careerquicker than anybody expected.The Vikings signed Wentz as a backup last season, and did the same this offseason. It’s a good thing they did. At one point in this NFC North battle, the Packers had a 22-10 lead, and then the Wentz-led Vikings scored 29 unanswered points in 17:08 of game clock. Wentz finished the day with 12 completions on 19 attempts for 133 yards, three touchdowns, no interceptions and a passer rating of 123.5. Wentz had a lot of help from his defense, but he also made some bang-on throws, and maybe he’s the unexpected quarterback reclamation project of the 2026 season.We’ve seen stranger things.-- It will be a while before we know whether the two most prominent trades of the 2026 offseason will bear fruit. On Sunday morning,ESPN reportedthat Los Angeles Rams edge-rusher Myles Garrett will undergo arthroscopic knee surgery and is out for at least four games. In his Rams debut,a 27-7 blowout loss to the San Francisco 49ers, Garrett was relatively muted, with no sacks and three quarterback pressures in 28 pass-rushing snaps. The Rams have the New York Giants, Broncos, Philadelphia Eagles and Bills to deal with over the next four weeks – without Garrett and superlative pass-rusher Jared Verse, who was dealt to Cleveland in the Garrett trade. It’s a blow to a Rams “Dream Team” who were set up for dominance before the games were actually played.-- The New England Patriots picked up former Eagles receiver AJ Brown this offseason to upgrade a formerly underwhelming group of targets for Drake Maye. But they were only able to see Brown for 31 snaps in their opener against the Seattle Seahawks before he suffered a high ankle sprain that will sideline him for up to six weeks.Brown caught just three passes on four targets for 26 yards in New England’s 13-10 loss, and now the Patriots will need to survive without him for a while. As always, it’s good to remember that football games are not played on paper.Explore more on these topicsBuffalo BillsNFLUS sportsfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Premier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s action | Soccer | The Guardian
description: Controversy rules the Manchester derby, Coventry are dunked on and Tottenham still can’t score a goal
Author: Guardian sport
Headline: Controversy rules the Manchester derby, Coventry are dunked on and Tottenham still can’t score a goal
Content: Manchester United manager Michael Carrick, Brighton scorer Lewis Dunk and Nottingham Forest’s James McAtee.Composite: Guardian Pictures (via Tom Jenkins; Shutterstock)View image in fullscreenManchester United manager Michael Carrick, Brighton scorer Lewis Dunk and Nottingham Forest’s James McAtee.Composite: Guardian Pictures (via Tom Jenkins; Shutterstock)Ten talking points from the weekend footballSoccerPremier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s actionControversy rules the Manchester derby, Coventry are dunked on and Tottenham still can’t score a goalGuardian sportMon 14 Sep 2026 03.00 EDTLast modified on Mon 14 Sep 2026 06.04 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on Google1Carrick fails to take advantage …The 199th Manchester derby was defined by two refereeing decisions: Phil Foden’s first-half red card for kicking out at Bruno Fernandes, and the intervention by the video assistant referee to award Erling Haaland’s winning goal despite Enzo Fernández appearing to interfere with play from an offside position. In both cases, a healthy dose of common sense might have led to a different outcome and Pro Ref admitted that Haaland’s goal should not have stood. Still, it is tough to argue that the final result was harsh on United. Foden’s dismissal gave the hosts a huge opportunity they failed to take, their best chance falling to Bryan Mbeumo in stoppage time. Michael Carrick began his reign witha 2-0 home derby winagainst 11 men in January, so this felt like a backward step for the manager, unable to find a way to control the game. Carrick also bemoaned City’s two days of extra rest after Champions League games, but chose to keep Fernandes and others on for 90 minutesin the 4-0 stroll past Sabah. United’s next two league games are away at Fulham and at home to Spurs. Carrick will need to be smarter to stop an early-season wobble becoming something more serious.Niall McVeigh2… while Maresca’s master plan pays offFoden’s red card also posed a big test for Enzo Maresca, overseeing his first derby asManchester Citymanager. After a solid but unspectacular start to the league season, this could have become a painful afternoon with his team down to 10 men. Instead, the Italian made smart decisions to secure a galvanising result and keep pace with Arsenal, both teams already edging clear of their expected rivals. Maresca made just one change in the first 80 minutes, but bringing on Iliman Ndiaye for Rayan Cherki gave his team a more direct threat on the break. Fellow new signings Enzo Fernández and Elliot Anderson have settled quickly, the latter imperious in midfield during a second half where City rarely looked short-handed. At the back, Marc Guéhi barely put a foot wrong as City showed a solidity that had been lacking. The manner of Haaland’s winner was fortunate, to say the least, but the visitors’ second-half display deserved all three points.NMcMatch report:Manchester United 0-1 Manchester CityView image in fullscreenEnzo Maresca celebrates with Ruben Días after a statement win for Manchester City.Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian3Free-scoring Seagulls dunk on CoventryOn another day, any of the excellent individual goals from Charalampos Kostoulas, Malick Yalcouyé and Yasin Ayari could have been the showstopper in Brighton’s rout of Coventry. But none could compare with Lewis Dunk’s sensational 35-yard pile-driver into the top corner. For a centre-back to even consider shooting from where he did is ridiculous, but Dunk insisted he has “that sort of shot in my locker”, with Fabian Hürzeler saying everyone at the club knows all about the shooting technique he possesses. Dunk was one of five goalscorers on Sunday as Brighton continue to show they can do things differently to last season, when Danny Welbeck was their chief attacking threat with 13 Premier League goals. Eight players have scored in four league games and who really needs a star striker when your centre-back can hit a ball like that?Ben BloomMatch report:Coventry 0-5 Brighton4Arteta’s ‘sadness’ unfair to SunderlandReferees are supposed to be clamping down on grappling, holding and shirt-pulling at dead balls this season, but until the 58th minute at the Stadium of Light on SaturdaySunderlandand Arsenal got away with plenty at corners and throws. The irony was that when John Brooks penalised Ezri Konsa for hauling Dan Ballard down at a throw and awarded Sunderland a penalty, subsequently endorsed by a VAR check, it proved contentious. There was a strong case for arguing that Ballard’s clever “judo roll” had landed the admittedly far from innocent Konsa in deep trouble. No matter that David Raya’s brilliant save ensured Enzo Le Fée’s penalty proved academic; Mikel Arteta subsequently cut a study in righteous indignation. Going over the top, he said he felt “sad” for football and talked about wanting to “protect the game”. When, two minutes after Le Fée’s miss, Bruno Guimarães curled in a superlative shot Arsenal were en route to a 2-0 win sealed by Bukayo Saka’s late penalty and their immaculate start to the season continued. Sunderland, though, had played well and deserved more credit from a less than magnanimous Arteta.Louise TaylorMatch report:Sunderland 0-2 ArsenalView image in fullscreen‘A study in righteous indignation’: Mikel Arteta talks to fourth official Elliot Bell.Photograph: Scott Heppell/Reuters5Midfield fragility haunts IraolaAndoni Iraola will inevitably discover some unwelcome truths in the learning stage of hisLiverpoolreign. A second successive Premier League draw at Anfield – their seventh from 12 games in 2026 – revealed several, from Kostas Tsimikas’s unreliability as a starter to the porous nature of a central midfield pairing of Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai. Iraola had to make changes given the tight turnaround from Wednesday’s Champions League win over Atlético Madrid, his first experience of having to do so with Liverpool, and the absence of Alexis Mac Allister had more of a destabilising effect than he might have imagined. Gravenberch and Szoboszlai offered minimal resistance to a Fulham team that cut through with ease and, together with Florian Wirtz, offered little to an ineffective Liverpool attack assembled at huge expense. There will be further changes when Tottenham visit in the Carabao Cup on Tuesday. Teenage midfielder Trey Nyoni, impressive in pre-season, should get an opportunity to show he can be a viable alternative the next time Mac Allister is rested.Andy HunterMatch report:Liverpool 0-0 Fulham6Miss and Tel: De Zerbi’s Spurs still scorelessRoberto De Zerbi insisted there “is not a problem” between him and Mathys Tel, when nobody had seriously suggested there was. “I love Mathys as a player, as a guy,” the Tottenham manager said. Still, it was not a good day for Tel againstEverton. Dropped from the starting XI, he received an on-pitch tutorial from De Zerbi in how to play as a No 9. The Tottenham manager had moved Tel there in the closing stages after initially introducing him in his favoured left-wing role. Play on the shoulder, attack the six-yard box, was the gist of De Zerbi’s advice. Spurs’ toothlessness at the sharp end of their formation was not on Tel. The real worry was Dominic Solanke and how he ghosted through another Premier League game. Omar Marmoush was also ineffective; first on the left, then briefly as the No 9 after Solanke was withdrawn. Solanke has been undermined by injuries, but 12 league goals since his £55m arrival in August 2024 is not good enough.David Hytnerskip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionMatch report:Tottenham 0-0 EvertonView image in fullscreenTottenham manager Roberto De Zerbi gives Mathys Tel his post-game review on the pitch.Photograph: Andrew Couldridge/Action Images/Reuters7Sage wisdom under scrutiny at PalaceCrystal Palace’s defenders committed the cardinal sin of not playing to the whistle when they allowed Ipswich to equalise during the first half of Saturday’s costly 3-2 defeat. It was just the latest example of the bad habits that are creeping in since Pierre Sage’s arrival as manager. While the Frenchman promised to speak to Axel Disasi after his reckless red card in the first half cost Palace dear, it was surprising to hear Sage say: “I had this discussion with them because they did the same thing in a session. I told them to continue to play. Because of the VAR now, I prefer they deflect the ball [out] for a corner and then ask the referee if they were offside or not.” Palace are lacking leadership at the back after selling Maxence Lacroix to Chelsea and have conceded seven goals in their first two matches at home. Sage must find a solution to their defensive woes without Disasi, who will miss their next three Premier League matches due to suspension.Ed AaronsMatch report:Crystal Palace 2-3 Ipswich8Chelsea’s defence remains unseriousChelsea do not relish the art of defending enough. Hull’s first goal on Saturday was a case in point. Malo Gusto was outmuscled by Ryan Giles and Mohamed Belloumi equalised when Jorrel Hato misjudged the Hull left-back’s cross. Xabi Alonso called it soft. TheChelseamanager replaced Hato at half-time, but the problems are not down to one individual. Emiliano Martínez, signed as Robert Sanchez’s replacement, is yet to convince in goal. Wesley Fofana still flatters to deceive, Levi Colwill is feeling his way back from injury and Maxence Lacroix was surprisingly on the bench against Hull. Chelsea have conceded 12 goals in Alonso’s first six games in all competitions. They remain unserious.Jacob SteinbergMatch report:Chelsea 2-2 HullView image in fullscreenThe Chelsea captain, Reece James, looks forlorn after Hull City’s second goal at Stamford Bridge.Photograph: Peter Cziborra/Action Images/Reuters9McAtee finally finds his feet at ForestOliver Glasner consistently name-checked James McAtee before a ball was kicked this season, adamant the £30m arrival from Manchester City last summer could finally make a splash in aNottingham Forestshirt. His performance in their first victory of the season, at Aston Villa on Saturday, was further evidence of a player revitalised. Glasner is convinced the 23-year-old can thrive in the quarterback role he gave Adam Wharton at Crystal Palace. McAtee has started all four league matches this season, twice as many as he managed in the last campaign; he was hooked at half-time in successive starts against Utrecht and Wrexham either side of the turn of the year. But against Villa, McAtee oozed confidence and relished dictating the game. Glasner represents McAtee’s fifth Forest manager in 13 months, but in the Austrian he has one of his biggest fans.Ben FisherMatch report:Aston Villa 1-2 Nottingham Forest10Rose still winless despite positive signs“Many teams struggle againstBournemouth,” said Brentford’s Vitaly Janelt. That has been true of all four opponents faced in Marco Rose’s Premier League tenure. And yet the wait for a first win continues. “If you watch our games, I think it’s a joy,” said Rose. This week, his squad jets off to face Real Sociedad in the Europa League, fulfilling the dream of fans and the club’s owner. Bill Foley. Rose, one of the game’s optimists, refused to cast blame on Djordje Petrovic’s goalkeeping errors for Kevin Schade’s double, instead looking ahead to Thursday: “A special night for the club against top opposition. It’s a tough stadium. Top atmosphere, intense opponent, a good team with Spanish national team players.” Bournemouth may well find life easier in Europe. As Justin Kluivert said: “It’s lovely to play in this team. We are front-footed, we press, we don’t just let it be a slow game, we go for it.”John BrewinMatch report:Bournemouth 2-2 BrentfordPosTeamPGDPts1Arsenal47122Man City46123Hull4384Brighton4875Chelsea4176Brentford4367Liverpool4268Everton4269Ipswich4-3610Newcastle32511Leeds31512Nottm Forest40513Man Utd40414Sunderland4-2415AFC Bournemouth4-1316Crystal Palace4-5317Tottenham Hotspur4-5218Fulham4-3119Aston Villa4-6120Coventry4-100Explore more on these topicsFootballTen talking points from the weekend footballArsenalAston VillaBournemouthBrentfordBrighton & Hove AlbionChelseafeaturesShareReuse this content

title: USA’s Solheim Cup inquest begins amid early celebrations and stats complaints | Solheim Cup | The Guardian
description: Angela Stanford, the USA captain, was frustrated by the lack of in-play statistics and has offered a warning to her Ryder Cup counterpart Jim Furyk
Author: Ewan Murray
Headline: Angela Stanford, the USA captain, was frustrated by the lack of in-play statistics and has offered a warning to her Ryder Cup counterpart Jim Furyk
Content: Angela Stanford, the USA captain, looks on during the 15-13 Solheim Cup defeat against Europe.Photograph: Naomi Baker/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenAngela Stanford, the USA captain, looks on during the 15-13 Solheim Cup defeat against Europe.Photograph: Naomi Baker/Getty ImagesSolheim CupUSA’s Solheim Cup inquest begins amid early celebrations and stats complaintsLosing captain frustrated by lack of in-play statisticsStanford offers warning to Ryder Cup leader Jim FurykEwan MurrayMon 14 Sep 2026 10.15 EDTLast modified on Mon 14 Sep 2026 16.46 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe latest inquest into failure by an American team on European soil involves slow greens, the perception of a premature celebration and a curious absence of statistical backup. Angela Stanford, whoseSolheim Cupteam were defeated by Europe in the Netherlands on Sunday, warned Jim Furyk’s Ryder Cup contingent to take note.Stanford used the numbers-based evidence of Justin Ray to assist with decision-making and Furyk will do likewise at Adare Manor next year. In the aftermath of the 15-13 defeat and assessing Ray’s input, Stanford clearly had an underlying gripe. “I’m wondering how honest to be,” she said.Europe win Solheim Cup against USA to give captain Anna Nordqvist last laughRead more“Justin Ray is extremely helpful. We were missing some pieces this week. Like, in Spain [in 2023] we had people giving us strokes gained in each match, even in practice. And we didn’t have that this year.“Because I know he’s working with Jim in the Ryder Cup, just now in the locker room, I told him exactly what he needed to do for Jim. Those things do matter and Justin was a huge help. He got us to this point.“It’s easy to get blown out over here. So I think we had the right formula and he helped us make that formula, so Justin Ray is awesome.”Pressed on why there was not the adequate backup resource she had referenced, Stanford said: “We just didn’t. See, that’s why I couldn’t be so honest with you.”It should be remembered that the teams were level, at 8-8, before a Sunday singles session where the USA team stood as the favourites. Following Stanford’s logic, she appears to be implying her team were denied the opportunity to take a lead into day three.Saturday’s conclusion had felt significant. Extraordinary pieces of play by Jennifer Kupcho on the last two holes meant she and Lindy Duncan claimed an unlikely point against Carlota Ciganda and Céline Boutier. Social media lit up with video of the USA team celebrating with beers on the bus back to their hotel. “They drink on Saturday, we drink on Sunday,” Europe’s team chanted when they made the same journey a day later.Stanford disputed any sense of untimely euphoria. She had been unwilling to ask the American players to tone down their joy. “That’s kind of tricky because you don’t ever want to take away from that moment,” she said. “The worst thing I could have done is go in there and be like: ‘OK, y’all. Come off this high.’ You don’t want to take away from those moments. We’re never going to see anything like that again.“I think they handled it very well. We’ve never seen that so we don’t really know how to react. I talked to Kupcho and everybody and they’re like, ‘Yeah, we got good rest, but it did take a minute to come off because it was a pretty high, high.’”Another element was the putting surfaces. Anna Nordqvist, Europe’s captain, shrugged off any notion of gamesmanship by pointing out “we are in Europe in September”, but the pace of the greens had caught out the USA team.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |FortnightlySign up toThe HotspotA new fortnightly newsletter covering the intersection of sport and the climate crisisEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotion“Apparently I didn’t get to know the [greens] superintendent as well as I should have,” Stanford said only half in jest. “Even when we showed up in July here, they were faster. And I don’t think it had anything to do with the rain either.View image in fullscreenAnna Nordqvist, the Europe captain, lifts the Solheim Cup.Photograph: Naomi Baker/Getty Images“Now, saying that, it’s my responsibility to get the team ready. This is the one thing I am kicking myself [about], is that I just didn’t keep pushing, ‘We [have] got to figure out how to hit our putts a little bit harder.’ Which is really difficult, to change the way you putt.“I’m a little frustrated with myself. Nobody complained about it at all. It’s me saying this right now that I wish I would have maybe hammered it home more; they’re going to be slow, they’re going to be slow, they’re going to be slow. We don’t play on greens this slow usually.”There is more than enough blame to go around, it seems.Explore more on these topicsSolheim CupGolfUS sportsnewsShareReuse this content

title: PSG have finally won a game in Ligue 1 – but they were far from convincing | Ligue 1 | The Guardian
description: Ferran Torres has been brilliant for his new club with most of his new PSG teammates floundering for form
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Ferran Torres has been brilliant for his new club with most of his new PSG teammates floundering for form
Content: Ferran Torres scored the only goal of the game as PSG beat Brest; his sixth in five appearances for his new club.Photograph: Xavier Laine/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenFerran Torres scored the only goal of the game as PSG beat Brest; his sixth in five appearances for his new club.Photograph: Xavier Laine/Getty ImagesGuardian Sport NetworkLigue 1PSG have finally won a game in Ligue 1 – but they were far from convincingFerran Torres has been brilliant for his new club with most of his new teammates floundering for formByGet French Football NewsLuke EntwistleMon 14 Sep 2026 07.35 EDTLast modified on Mon 14 Sep 2026 13.16 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleIt was just a flicker. Ferran Torres picks the ball up and passes it to João Neves. The Portugal midfielder plays it into Ousmane Dembélé, who has lured in Raphaël Le Guen and eliminates him with a mesmeric first-time back-heel into the path of Torres.TheBrestdefence are just cones in a training drill, mere extras in this work of art as the Spaniard glides back into the scene to pass the ball into Egil Selvik’s bottom-left corner from 25 yards; it happened in slow motion, but was too quick for the Norwegian goalkeeper to react.Top of the table, empty in the stands: inside the revolt against Lazio’s owner | Nicky BandiniRead moreIt is a move that had the slick and elegant fluidity of what we have come to expect fromParis Saint-Germain. Just four minutes in, the champions were ahead and the Stade Francis Le-Blé anticipated a show of force, a statement from their visitors.Luis Enrique had described PSG’s start to the Ligue 1 season as catastrophic. A comfortable 6-1 win againstSlovan Bratislava in the Champions Leaguelast Wednesday signalled a welcome return to form. The Sopposition manager, none other than Yaya Touré, described his opponents on the night as a machine – we have heard that before.But once again, PSG were defective in Brittany on Sunday night, even if they did leave with all three points. Torres’s sublime finish was the only goal of the game. It was the Spaniard’s sixth since joining from Barcelona in the summer. All of his six efforts on target this season have found the net. He is clearly still riding the crest of a wave of confidence, having scored the winner inthe World Cup final.Torres’s supreme confidence is not shared by his teammates. Vitinha in particular has yet to resurface since the summer break and PSG are suffering from the lack of incision he usually provides. Khvicha Kvaratskhelia is not quite back to his usual levels either and going into this game, there were creeping doubts about Matvey Safonov in goal. The Russian was at fault last weekend when Stanis Idumbo finished at his near post to secure a win for Monaco. It was at his near post he conceded to Kai Havertz in theChampions League finalin May; if there is a weakness in PSG, Safonov was the most likely candidate.But it is only thanks to him that PSG ended a run of five games without a win against French opponents. He was not forced into action when Nuno Mendes played Kamory Doumbia in one-on-one in the second half, the Mali international striking the outside of the PSG post.Safonov did get a strong hand down low to his left when Doumbia rose highest to thunder a header towards goal and in the dying stages Pathé Mboup’s curled effort to the far post was tipped around the corner.View image in fullscreenGoalkeeper Matvey Safonov kept PSG in the game with a number of saves.Photograph: Xavier Laine/Getty ImagesBrest finished with a higher xG than the European champions, but had no points to show for it. Moments of brilliance in both areas were the difference. But that is what PSG are confined to at the minute: moments, flickers of brilliance.“It was the worst of our fourLigue 1matches, even if we won,” said Luis Enrique. “In the other three matches, we showed a high level at the back, but our opponents scored every chance. This time, it was the opposite.”Alarm bells are not ringing. PSG often start slowly and it is only the quality of opposition faced at the start of the last campaign that ensured there was not such a significant deficit to the leaders. They are five points behind Lille, Monaco andRennes, all of whom are on 10 points.Last week, Marquinhos said that it was “a matter of ambition and motivation” as PSG hoped to replicate the success of the past two seasons. Just like Torres’s passed finish, PSG are all about timing and they have a knack for peaking at the right moment.The Hotspot | South Korea pushes for football season to make winter switch after unbearable summerRead moreThere were no doubts Brest were up to the occasion. The Stade Francis Le-Blé was a cauldron of emotion as Eric Roy was commemorated. The Brest manager, who guided the clubinto European competition for the first time, in 2024, died in June due to pancreatic cancer that began when he was appointed as the club’s manager in January 2023. His diagnosis was never made public.Roy’s daughter, Victoria-Rose, spoke on the pitch before the match, “King Eric” shirts were worn on the sidelines and there were further moments of commemoration in the stands throughout the game. Hugo Magnetti said they had played for Roy. “He would have been proud of us, but he would have also ticked us off for missing some big chances.”The game, at times, felt like a subplot, but what happened in it was not inconsequential. Some of those fears about waning “ambition and motivation” were deepened, as was a crisis of confidence among some of PSG’s key players, despite victory. But there were also flickers of brilliance Luis Enrique must hope will become more enduring as the season progresses.Quick GuideLigue 1 resultsShowLille 2-0 TroyesLe Mans 2-2 LensBrest 0-1 PSGStrasbourg 1-1 MonacoAuxerre 1-0 NiceLe Havre 0-0 AngersLorient 2-2 ToulouseParis FC 0-0 LyonRennes 1-0 MarseilleWas this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.Talking pointsWill Still andAuxerrehave their first points on the board thanks to their young English forward Cameron Archer. The Southampton loanee made his debut last weekend and scored a stunner in a 3-1 defeat to Lyon. This weekend he scored the only goal of the game against Nice. The win drags Auxerre off the bottom of the table – a place now occupied by their opponents on the day. Nice, without a win, have scored once in their first four matches. Their coach, Olivier Pantaloni, says there are traces of last season’s difficult campaign lingering in the minds of his players. They must quickly dispel them in order to avoid a repeat.Four games in and the temperature is already rising inMarseille. The season started well, with a 4-0 home win to Strasbourg on opening day, but they have since lost to Monaco, Paris FC and Rennes. There is no real shame in any of those defeats; the matches were close and the opponents are expected to be in the race for Europe. “We can rival these teams but not yet beat them,” said Bruno Génésio after the 1-0 defeat at Rennes on Friday. Génésio added it was not up to him to state the club’s objectives this season – a clear message to his superiors. “We may need to explain things more clearly Maybe we have to say it so that people can understand.” The lack of quality and depth in the squad says enough; Marseille are outsiders in the race for European football.PosTeamPGDPts1Lille45102Monaco44103Rennes43104Lyon4485Paris FC4486Strasbourg4177PSG4058Brest4059Lorient40510Lens41411Angers4-1412Troyes4-5413Marseille40314Le Mans4-1315Auxerre4-6316Le Havre4-2217Toulouse4-3218Nice4-42This is an article byGet French Football NewsExplore more on these topicsLigue 1Guardian Sport NetworkEuropean club footballParis Saint-GermainBrestAuxerreMarseilleRennesfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Haaland goal should not have stood but VAR made the right call with Sunderland penalty | Referees | The Guardian
description: Matt Donohue is only human and made a mistake, but, in general, referees have started well this season
Author: Chris Foy
Headline: Matt Donohue is only human and made a mistake, but, in general, referees have started well this season
Content: Players wait for the referee Michael Oliver to reveal the VAR decision, which incorrectly awarded Manchester City the goal by Erling Haaland.Photograph: Catherine Ivill/AMA/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenPlayers wait for the referee Michael Oliver to reveal the VAR decision, which incorrectly awarded Manchester City the goal by Erling Haaland.Photograph: Catherine Ivill/AMA/Getty ImagesRefereesAnalysisHaaland goal should not have stood but VAR made the right call with Sunderland penaltyChris FoyMatt Donohue is only human and made a mistake, but, in general, referees have started well this seasonMon 14 Sep 2026 15.00 EDTLast modified on Mon 14 Sep 2026 21.30 EDTShareThere was a disappointing outcome on a big decision in the Manchester derby and no one will feel it more than the video assistant referee, Matt Donohue. On Sunday night, Pro Ref confirmed that Donohue had made a mistake in allowing Erling Haaland’s goal inCity’s 1-0 victoryto stand when Enzo Fernández had been in an offside position.When a VAR considers a decision such as this they start from the point at which the goal is scored and work backwards. Here, when Haaland scores, the flag is raised by the assistant referee for offside. The VAR automatically checked that on-field decision and used a semi‑automated system to show Haaland was onside. The decision was then made to overturn the call and award the goal.‘An error of judgement’: Pro Ref admits mistake in awarding Haaland’s derby winnerRead moreBefore Haaland scores, however, an offside Fernández, marked by Lisandro Martínez, has challenged for the crossed ball with a diving header. The VAR needs to look at this aspect and make a two-part assessment. The first question is: does Fernández make a clear attempt to play the ball? The second: did that action affect the ability of Martínez to defend the cross? In this case, the answer to both questions was yes. The goal should not have been awarded.I think Donohue looked at the Fernández situation and did not recognise it was an offence. He is a highly skilled VAR but referees are human and the fact he has got it wrong will hurt. He will learn from it but I would defend the performance of referees more broadly this season.We’re 39 games into the campaign and they have started really well. We’ve seen some very good examples of officials dealing with holding offences, the ball is in play for longer and referees are managing goal-kicks and throw‑ins too. More stuff is thrown at them every season to deal with.In the game atManchester United, Haaland’s goal wasn’t the only incident to cause debate with a real split of opinion on what sanctions should have been imposed. With regards to the coming together between Bruno Fernandes and Phil Foden, which led to the City player being sent off, I’ve heard two reds, two yellows and two dustings down.View image in fullscreenPatrick Dorgu plays the ball to Erling Haaland with Enzo Fernández clearly offside.Photograph: Sky SportsLet’s be clear: Foden sticks his studs into Fernandes’s midriff after the United captain had kicked at him with a toe. Michael Oliver shows Foden a deserved red card for violent conduct. Fernandes had provoked Foden by moving his right toe into Foden’s backside but in my opinion, had Oliver seen it, he would have given Fernandes a yellow card because it was a pretty petulant act of unsporting behaviour. Whereas Foden’s kick was violent conduct, I would argue Fernandes’s was not.The laws on violent conduct describe when a player “uses or attempts to use excessive force or brutality against an opponent when not challenging for the ball”. Did Foden use excessive force or brutality against an opponent? I think he did. But Fernandes didn’t. There was no brutality in that. There was no force. Clearly, the referee didn’t see the act of petulance but in terms of the bigger decision the officials got it correct. Even Enzo Maresca said in his press conference that Foden was rightly sent off.The previous day there was another incident with lots of noise around it: thedecision to award Sunderland a penaltyagainst Arsenal. Dan Ballard and Ezri Konsa go to ground in the Arsenal box and the verdict from John Brooks was penalty kick. You could quite clearly see that Konsa was holding Ballard and really focusing only on his opponent and not the ball. The VAR, Stuart Attwell, then checked the decision and had to determine whether the referee made a clear and obvious error.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionBallard has got a little bit of Konsa’s shirt too and there’s a bit of tugging but that in itself, with all the bits and bobs going on, doesn’t jump out as a clear and obvious error, so they stay with the on-field decision. What is important to note is the light touch from VARs this season.Lots of people will say penalty. Others will say not for me. Attwell was right to say check complete, confirming the penalty. If a penalty hadn’t been awarded, however, there would have been no intervention either because it’s not a clear and obvious error. It’s what we would term a check complete either way.Chris Foy is a former Premier League refereeExplore more on these topicsRefereesVideo assistant referees (VARs)Manchester CityManchester UnitedLaws of footballanalysisShareReuse this content

title: De Zerbi backs ‘sensitive guy’ Solanke to find form before tricky Anfield trip | Tottenham Hotspur | The Guardian
description: Tottenham visit Liverpool in the Carabao Cup third round, having failed to win in 17 visits and failed to score a league goal this season
Author: David Hytner
Headline: Tottenham visit Liverpool in the Carabao Cup third round, having failed to win in 17 visits and failed to score a league goal this season
Content: Spurs paid Bournemouth £55m for Dominic Solanke in 2024.Photograph: Marc Atkins/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenSpurs paid Bournemouth £55m for Dominic Solanke in 2024.Photograph: Marc Atkins/Getty ImagesTottenham HotspurDe Zerbi backs ‘sensitive guy’ Solanke to find form before tricky Anfield tripTottenham visit Liverpool in Carabao Cup third roundRicharlison will play no part despite being eligibleDavid HytnerMon 14 Sep 2026 17.30 EDTLast modified on Mon 14 Sep 2026 21.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleRoberto De Zerbi has no doubt Dominic Solanke will rediscover his best levels as the head coach made clear he had left no stone unturned in the mission to solve Tottenham’s goalscoring problem.Spurs go to Liverpool in theCarabao Cupon Tuesday after the 0-0 home draw with Everton in the Premier League on Saturday; they have not found the net in their four matches in the competition. Tottenham did beat Charlton 5-1 at home in the second round of the Carabao Cup.Premier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s actionRead moreSolanke is the only forward in De Zerbi’s squad to have enjoyed a prolific season in England’s top division; he scored 19 times for Bournemouth in 2023-24, which convinced Tottenham to pay £55m for him. The 29-year-old has 22 additional goals in the Premier League, 12 of them for Spurs. De Zerbi has Omar Marmoush, who scored seven times in the league for Manchester City in the second half of 2024-25 after joining from Eintracht Frankfurt in January. That apart, the pickings for De Zerbi’s attacking players have been slim in the competition.Solanke, whose pre-season was undermined by an injury sustained on the club’s tour of New Zealand and Australia, was ineffective against Everton and a target for criticism is some quarters. De Zerbi will keep the faith. He remembers being amazed at how well Solanke played for Bournemouth against his Brighton team in September 2023. Brighton won 3-1 but Solanke scored. De Zerbi knows that when Solanke is fully fit the goals and performances will follow. He intends to involve the formerLiverpoolstriker at Anfield, whether from the start or as a substitute.“Dom is a sensitive guy,” De Zerbi said. “He needs to feel full confidence – and from myself, he has big, big confidence. I believe he can score 10-15 goals, for sure. He’s already scored in Bournemouth so why not he can score in Tottenham? It’s the same sport.“[He is] sensitive because he’s a smart guy. Sensitive guys are smart. Maybe [he has had] many injuries, maybe he doesn’t feel in the best physical condition, maybe he would like to do something different on the pitch. But now he’s not fit yet. He has to play. It can be important for him [at Anfield]. And then I think he comes back to the player who was in Bournemouth. I remember Brighton v Bournemouth in the Amex Stadium; he was incredible. I said to my assistant: ‘Who is this striker?’”View image in fullscreenDominic Solanke scores Tottenham’s second goal in their 5-1 Carabao Cup second round victory over Charlton.Photograph: John Walton/PADe Zerbi continues to try to bond his players away from the pitch. He said he had again taken them for dinner in Mayfair last week and paid the bill. “As long as I keep some money for my cigarettes, then no problem,” he said with a smile.De Zerbi is leaning heavily into video analysis, going through clips from matches in team meetings and giving the players individual ones to study. There has been an emphasis in training on attacking crosses in the right way and regaining possession in the final third. The players have also stayed behind for extra shooting practice of their own volition, De Zerbi said.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotion“If we want to change from the last two or three seasons we have to be stronger here,” he said, pointing to his head. “We have to believe in the quality of the players and the decisions we made one month ago. Or we change. You can change players or change coaches … change, change, change and nothing changes. Or you stay with the head, stay humble and with the right spirit to work. I believe in my players. I hope they believe in themselves like I believe in them.”De Zerbi reported that Sandro Tonali would miss the Liverpool game with a knock, and Richarlison will not be involved despite being eligible for the Carabao Cup; the Brazilian forwardwas omitted from Spurs’ Premier League squad.Pedro Porro is still out but Destiny Udogie is back, and Mohammed Kudus is ready to start. James Maddison, though, is still unavailable. De Zerbi will make changes and he mentioned Marcos Senesi, Tosin Adarabioyo, Ben Davies, Lucas Bergvall and Mathys Tel as being in contention to come into the XI. Spurs have not won at Anfield in 17 matches.Explore more on these topicsTottenham HotspurRoberto De ZerbiLiverpoolCarabao CupnewsShareReuse this content

title: Andoni Iraola tells Liverpool forwards they must do more to make his system work | Liverpool | The Guardian
description: The head coach was critical of his forwards’ pressing in their Premier League stalemate agains Fulham at Anfield on Saturday
Author: Andy Hunter
Headline: The head coach was critical of his forwards’ pressing in their Premier League stalemate agains Fulham at Anfield on Saturday
Content: Alexander Isak, Bradley Barcola and Victor Muñoz (left to right) were three of the Liverpool forwards who failed to score against Fulham.Photograph: Matt McNulty/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenAlexander Isak, Bradley Barcola and Victor Muñoz (left to right) were three of the Liverpool forwards who failed to score against Fulham.Photograph: Matt McNulty/Getty ImagesLiverpoolAndoni Iraola tells Liverpool forwards they must do more to make his system workHead coach insists forwards need to improve pressingChanges up front likely for Carabao Cup tie against SpursAndy HunterMon 14 Sep 2026 11.55 EDTLast modified on Mon 14 Sep 2026 16.46 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleAndoni Iraola has shifted the focus on to Liverpool’s forwards for the team’suninspiring display against Fulham, insisting they need to give more to make his system work.The head coach admitted his team took “a step backwards” with their goalless draw on Saturday. His central midfield pairing of Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai struggled to contain their Fulham counterparts, winning two of five duels and one of nine duels respectively. But Iraola believes the problems started further forward with the pressing of Liverpool’s expensively assembled attack.Frustrated Liverpool lack any spark as Fulham claim deserved first pointRead more“It’s not a matter of just the midfielders,” he said. “When we have been good collectively the mid­fielders have looked a lot better and recovered more balls. It’s not because they are winning duels that they play better, it’s because we are helping them more to win the duels.“If the ones up front do their job very well then the defenders and midfielders look good. If we are allowing them to defend one v one all the time and we are not aggressive, then our defenders will also struggle. If the players ahead of you are doing their job then you look a better midfielder or defender because you win more easier duels, you have more chance of winning one. It is more collective.“It isn’t about changing this player for that player. That’s the help we have to give to our defenders and midfielders so everyone looks better, looks smarter and are in better positions.”Iraola is unlikely to field the same frontline of Alexander Isak, Bradley Barcola, Florian Wirtz and Víctor Muñoz when Tottenham visit Anfield in the Carabao Cup third round on Tuesday. Trey Nyoni is pressing for a start in midfield and Iraola confirmed that Giorgi Mamardashvili, whom he tried to sign for Bournemouth, would replace ­Alisson in goal.View image in fullscreenThe Liverpool goalkeeper Giorgi Mamardashvili will make his first appearance of the season in the Carabao Cup tie against Tottenham.Photograph: Liverpool FC/Getty ImagesOn the issues of Saturday, which contributed to a third draw in four Premier League games, he also said: “Compared to previous games, we won the ball a lot lower in the pitch. We don’t concede a lot, and the only big chance we conceded was our goal‑kick that we messed up. But we were recovering the ball always very low and when that happens you have to attack against 11 players and that makes it more difficult to make the difference.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotion“In previous games we could win it a lot higher and use our quick transitions to attack against less players and use the space better. That is key to our system. We need to recover the ball as high as possible because it makes the offensive side a lot easier, and we have more situations to attack in one v one.”Explore more on these topicsLiverpoolAndoni IraolaFulhamnewsShareReuse this content

title: ‘Very weak. Very bad’: how Rodri’s verdict exposed woeful Valencia’s crisis | La Liga | The Guardian
description: The World Cup winner’s off-the-cuff assessment was brutally honest. Within days their manager and CEO were gone, but the problems run deeper than either man
Author: Sid Lowe
Headline: The World Cup winner’s off-the-cuff assessment was brutally honest. Within days their manager and CEO were gone, but the problems run deeper than either man
Content: Valencia fans hold up signs that read: ‘Lim, go home’ in a protest against the clubs president, Kiat Lim, during the match against Barcelona, which they lost 5-0.Photograph: David Ramos/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenValencia fans hold up signs that read: ‘Lim, go home’ in a protest against the clubs president, Kiat Lim, during the match against Barcelona, which they lost 5-0.Photograph: David Ramos/Getty ImagesLa Liga‘Very weak. Very bad’: how Rodri’s verdict exposed woeful Valencia’s crisisThe World Cup winner’s off-the-cuff assessment was brutally honest. Within days their manager and CEO were gone, but the problems run much deeperSid LoweMon 14 Sep 2026 12.10 EDTLast modified on Mon 14 Sep 2026 18.44 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleKiat Lim wanted to seeValenciaplay so badly, so that is what he did. It was week four in La Liga, 6 September, and for the first time since he was given the presidency 18 months earlier, the owner’s 33-year-old son was going to watch his team play a competitive game. He was going to do it from the inside, too, so he took a flight to Spain, landing at Manises in a black mask and cap, a van to the hotel, then the team bus to Mestalla. He looked through the window as they rolled along Avenida Suecia, a huge, noisy crowd waiting, but when he got off and headed through the iron gate with its ornate club badge, he saw that this was no welcome.Above him as he went in were giant portraits of Mario Kempes, Antonio Puchades, Juan Sol, Gaizka Mendieta, David Villa and Santiago Cañizares, footballers from a better time; around him were yellow banners and whistles for the footballers there now. Inside, Lim saw the game start with the lower south stand empty as fans stayed away until the 19th minute, the sound of another protest drifting in from the street. They were out there still when, sitting alongside Joan Laporta, he saw Lamine Yamal score the sixth-minute opener then get a second. And although that, also from Lamine Yamal, was ruled out, he eventually saw Barcelona get four more, presiding over a 5-0 debut defeat.He had seen supporters leave early, seen those that stayed turn towards him, chanting for him and his family to leave for good. He had seen the hankies come out and his players head into the tunnel heads bowed. He heard his manager insist that they were hurt but not sunk. What he did not see – what no one had seen yet but everyone would see soon enough – was the verdict from the bench.Withdrawn after an hour to a standing ovation, the World Cup winner Rodri took a towel and turned to Pau Cubarsí. “This lot are very weak, eh?” Spain’s captain said. “Very weak, mate. Very bad.” He asked where they finished last season, pulled a face that saidseriously?!when he was told just outside Europe, and noted that they had not left their own half. Valencia, he said, weremalísimo. Awful.View image in fullscreenRodri was caught on camera calling his former club ‘very weak’.Photograph: David Ramos/Getty ImagesThe sequence was caught on camera by El Día Después, and soon it was everywhere. Rodri called Valencia’s captain José Luis Gayà, saying sorry. After Barcelona’s Champions League win against Feyenoord three days later, he offered a public apology. It was, the Valencia coach, Carlos Corberán, said, a touch of self-preservation about his reaction, the least Rodri could do: apology accepted but his “unfortunate” words had “not been born of respect”. Yet there was no taunt, no mocking, no derision, no sign of a smile; instead there was a kind of shocked sadness. His words had not been thrown in anyone’s faces and were not for sharing. They were also true.And if Corberán noted that “Mestalla had applauded him too”, an aggravating factor, some of them would do it again: it had needed saying. Within a few days someone haddesigned T-shirtsdeclaring: “They’re very bad.” Underneath it read: “We’re all Rodri.” They had barely started printing off before Corberán was gone. Shoot the manager, not the messenger.Top of the table, empty in the stands: inside the revolt against Lazio’s owner | Nicky BandiniRead moreBarcelona’s victory over Valencia last Sunday was the third time in four games that they had scored five. Three days later they did it again. But those were not really the same – at Mestalla it was hard to avoid the feeling that Hansi Flick’s side could have scored 10 if they wanted to – and this was not just about Barcelona, this was about them. Valencia really aremalísimo.Four games into season, they had conceded nine and scored one – and that was a gift, scored by a man who is now seriously injured. They had a solitary point, were bottom, and things were not about to get any better. This Friday, they lost the Used To Be Big Derby, 1-0 to Sevilla at the Sanchez Pizjuan, Juan Iglesias’s header condemning Valencia to the worst start in their history and Corberán to the sack.There is something about these two; the last two times Sevilla fired their manager (García Pimienta and Matías Almeyda), it was after defeat to Valencia, while this is the third time Valencia fired a coach having lost at the Sánchez-Pizjuán: Quique Sánchez Flores in 2007, Nuno Espírito Santo in 2015 and now Corberán. Sánchez Flores got sacked at 4am. This time the wait was a little longer, if not much. When Valencia’s players and staff got back to Paterna to collect their cars in the small hours of Saturday, 100 fans waited to shout abuse and by the time training had finished there on Sunday morning the decision was made. Corberán was told during a video call from Singapore, Lim 10,000km away again.The coach who arrived in December 2024 with Valencia in the relegation zone and pulled them up to 12th; the manager who saw them slip into the relegation zone again at the halfway stage last season only to pull clear all the way to the edge of Europe, would not get the chance to try again. Just five weeks into the season, two months after his contract was extended for another year, and 10daysafter the CEO, Ron Gourlay, insisted that stability meant standing by a coach he believed in even if fans, some players and an increasingly belligerent media might not, he was gone.Mind you, Gourlay has gone too. At that defianttwo-hour, via-translator press conferenceGourlay insisted that if his critics were going to wait for him to go, their coffee would get cold, but he has been sacked along with all his staff. Braulio Vázquez, has joined from Osasuna – even though Braulio recently said Osasuna are the “only real club left” – given the task of finding a new coach, with the B team manager taking over for the time being. His arrival ushers in a restructuring and a “new era” at Valencia, the statement said.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Twice weeklySign up toSoccer DeskJonathan Wilson and Guardian journalists bring expert analysis and reporting on the biggest stories in soccer.Enter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionQuick GuideLa Liga resultsShowSevilla 1-0 ValenciaRacing Santander 2-1 AlavésOsasuna 0-2 EspanyolAthletic Bilbao 1-1 ElcheReal Madrid 4-1 Rayo VallecanoCelta Vigo 1-1 MálagaLevante 2-4 BarcelonaGetafe1-1 Deportivo A CoruñaWas this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.Braulio knows the club – he was sporting director there between 2011 and 2013 and his son is the left-back – and has been successful at Osasuna, widely considered a more convincing candidate than the man who was there until Sunday afternoon. Few fans are sorry to see Corberán go: in fact they have been chanting for just that, the social fracture another factor. A change of coach can change things, a change of CEO or sporting director too. Look at Valencia’s squad and they should and probably will be better than this, the academy keeps producing talent, and Mestalla still fills weekly. There are coaches out there that would convince, with Ernesto Valverde and Jagoba Arrasate’s names the first to be floated. They certainly couldn’t be much worse than they have been so far. But patience is thin and faith thinner, a pessimism long since having crept in, and not unjustifiably so.The only thing most fans want of the owners now is for them to leave which plays a part too, everyone caught in the never-ending tension. It is less than two years since Gourley took over, a year since Lim said that they have a “proper sporting plannow... which is not to say we did not in the past but now we have professionals in place.” He was already the sixth man to supposedly have responsibility for signings since Peter Lim bought the club in 2014. Óscar Sánchez will be Valencia’s fifteenth coach since then – and even Voro, the eternal caretaker who has had the job six times does not want it any more. Only Nuno and Marcelino have better win percentages than Corberán. This summer, they spent €9m (£7.7m);13clubs spent more. More than 20 players have come in and gone out in the last two years. Over the last seven seasons they have spent short of €70m; they have sold for more than €230m.View image in fullscreenCarlos Corberán was sacked by Valencia after their worst start to a season in their history.Photograph: Fran Santiago/Getty ImagesThere was a line in Rodri’s apology that talked about context and context is everything: Valencia being bad was not one Sunday; the fear is that it’s any given Sunday, that the days when they were good may be gone. He said that his comments were born of surprise, sadness, but the saddest thing is many weren’t surprised at all. This is what it is, they thought, grateful that someone else said it; forgive them if they do not foresee a way out. Yet if ambition must be adjusted it is hard not to hold on to what you were, your identity still, and maybe that’s a problem too. The Valencia Rodri returned to is not the Valencia he left behind. The year he went to England, they were a Champions League team; they have not made Europe since. And on Sunday he was right, Corberán taking the fall within a week.“We all want Valencia to get back to where they should be, one of the best clubs in our league,” Rodri said three days later, but he had already said enough, a truth told. Sitting in the stands, Lim had just about seen enough too.PosTeamPGDPts1Barcelona517152Real Madrid510123Alaves56104Atletico Madrid54105Sevilla52106Deportivo A Coruna5397Real Betis4098Espanyol5379Athletic Bilbao51710Racing Santander50711Osasuna5-3712Real Sociedad6-5713Levante5-2514Getafe5-3515Celta Vigo6-3416Rayo Vallecano5-6417Malaga5-6318Villarreal4-2219Elche5-7220Valencia5-91Explore more on these topicsLa LigaValenciaEuropean club footballfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: European football: Inter roar back to beat Udinese and join Roma at the top | European club football | The Guardian
description: Inter beat Udinese 5-3 and Roma won 2-0 at Torino to make it four wins from four for Serie A’s joint leaders
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Inter beat Udinese 5-3 and Roma won 2-0 at Torino to make it four wins from four for Serie A’s joint leaders
Content: Nicolò Barella (right) celebrates with Marcus Thuram after scoring Inter’s second goal against Udinese.Photograph: Claudia Greco/ReutersView image in fullscreenNicolò Barella (right) celebrates with Marcus Thuram after scoring Inter’s second goal against Udinese.Photograph: Claudia Greco/ReutersEuropean club footballEuropean football: Inter roar back to beat Udinese and join Roma at the topInter and Roma lead Serie A, Como move up to thirdReal Betis beat struggling Villarreal in La LigaAgenciesMon 14 Sep 2026 18.08 EDTLast modified on Mon 14 Sep 2026 18.31 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleInterfought back ⁠from two goals down ​to beatUdinese5-3 on Monday, maintaining their perfectSerie Astart alongsideRoma, who won 2-0 atTorinobefore Saturday’s match between ⁠the joint leaders. Both sides have 12 points from four matches and share top spot before their encounter at the Stadio Olimpico, whileComoare third on 10 points ⁠after beatingParma2-1.Calvert-Lewin shows the way as Leeds thrash limp Newcastle and rise to thirdRead moreUdinese stunned Inter with two goals in the opening 16 minutes, as James Abankwah headed home ​unmarked after nine minutes before Jurgen Ekkelenkamp doubled ‌the visitors’ lead with a ‌close-range finish seven minutes later. Inter hit back through Carlos Augusto, whose long-range effort flew into the bottom corner, ‌before Nicolò Barella levelled 10 minutes before half-time.The champions completed the turnaround in the 59th minute when Marcus Thuram netted from inside the box after Andy Diouf’s cutback from the byline. Francesco Esposito added a fourth and Ange-Yoan Bonny made it 5-2 with 11 minutes remaining. Udinese pulled one back in stoppage time through Idrissa Gueye, but it proved no more than a consolation.There was an injury concern for Inter as John Stones limped off with an apparent hamstring injury just after the hour mark. The England centre-back was making his first start after joining on a free transfer this summer.The Inter manager, Cristian Chivu, confirmed Stones would have to be fully assessed to determine the extent of the issue. “I don’t know, I haven’t had a chance to talk to him,” Chivu told Dazn. “I think he felt something on his flexor [muscle], and he will probably need to get some tests done.”View image in fullscreenRoma scorers Niccolò Pisilli and Donyell Malen celebrate at the final whistle.Photograph: Alessandro Di Marco/EPARomamade it four ‌wins from four thanks to goals from Donyell Malen and Niccolò Pisilli atTorino. Malen broke the deadlock five minutes before the interval after ​pouncing on a misplaced pass from goalkeeper Lucas Perri that had been intercepted by Paulo Dybala. Pisilli wrapped up the win in stoppage time, firing home from an angle after Gianluca Mancini kept the ball in play near the byline.TheRomacoach, Gian Piero Gasperini ,praised the understanding between Malen and Dybala. “Clearly, these are two players who are very talented ⁠individually, but they also complete each other as a pair. They combine beautifully ​to create goals in many games,” ​he told Dazn Italia.Comofollowed up their winning Champions League debut against RB Leipzig with a 2-1 home win overParma, with Jacobo Ramón and Kaiki Bruno scoring for Cesc Fàbregas’s side. “This is an important victory for me as a coach, because I am starting to realise what team we could become,” Fàbregas said.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionView image in fullscreenNatan (centre) and his Real Betis teammates  fought back from 1-0 down to beat Villarreal 2-1.Photograph: José Jordan/AFP/Getty ImagesMeanwhile in Spain,Real Betissecured a 2-1 win atVillarrealto move third in La Liga and leave their opponents in the relegation zone. Goals from Cucho Hernández and Natan helped Betis claim three points and pull level with Real Madrid, after Gerard Moreno opened the scoring for the home side.“Right now everything’s going against us, teams are punishing us,” Moreno told Movistar. “We have to stick together and demand more of ourselves … maybe when we go behind, anxiety kicks in and it’s more difficult. It’s hard to explain [how few] points we have... we have to be a team now more than ever.”Explore more on these topicsEuropean club footballInternazionaleUdineseRomaTorinoComoParmanewsShareReuse this content

title: WSL talking points: Olid must weather United storm, Arsenal wasteful again | Women's Super League | The Guardian
description: Manchester United need to regroup after a heavy home loss to Chelsea while Crystal Palace frustrated the Gunners
Author: Suzanne Wrack
Headline: Manchester United need to regroup after a heavy home loss to Chelsea while Crystal Palace frustrated the Gunners
Content: Crystal Palace’s goalkeeper Pauline Peyraud-Magnin, West Ham's Riko Ueki and Kelly Gago, the Manchester United head coach, Eva Olid.Composite: Getty; ShutterstockView image in fullscreenCrystal Palace’s goalkeeper Pauline Peyraud-Magnin, West Ham's Riko Ueki and Kelly Gago, the Manchester United head coach, Eva Olid.Composite: Getty; ShutterstockWomen's Super LeagueWSL talking points: Olid must weather United storm, Arsenal wasteful againManchester United need to regroup after a heavy home loss to Chelsea while Crystal Palace frustrated the GunnersSuzanne Wrack,Sophie DowneyandEmillia HawkinsMon 14 Sep 2026 07.17 EDTLast modified on Mon 14 Sep 2026 09.20 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleIs Olid under pressure?The frustration among Manchester United fans at full-time was evident at Leigh Sports Village after they had watched their team being thrashed 5-0 by a rampant Chelsea. There are certainly things to be worried about, but perhaps judging United’s new manager, Eva Olid, on the basis of how they performed against Sonia Bompastor’s established side is a little premature. The likelihood of United taking three points was always slim, despite the false hope afterChelsea’s 1-1 draw with Aston Villalast weekend. Chelsea have not been an easy opponent for the Red Devils, who have lost three WSL games by more than three goals, all against Chelsea. Having had three weeks with her side, Olid had a harsh WSL baptism with losses to London City Lionesses and Chelsea. United face Arsenal next. “These are difficult games to build the confidence in attack, but I’m here to build an identity and I have to be faithful to that,” said the Spaniard.Suzanne WrackMatch report: Manchester United 0-5 ChelseaArsenal lack finishing touch againThere was a strong sense of deja vu at the Emirates Stadium as Arsenal’s annual early season woes continued with goalless draw at home to Crystal Palace. For much of the game, it felt like they were re-winding the tape from seasons gone by, frustrated by resolute defensive visitors and their own lack of clinical finishing. Arsenal dominated every attacking metric – they had 79% possession, created 30 shots (nine on target) and recorded 70 touches in the Eagles’ area. The Gunners hit the woodwork twice, wasted golden opportunities and were denied by a standout performance from Pauline Peyraud-Magnin, who made eight saves. “Yes, there were good things, but it’s about scoring,” the head coach, Renée Slegers, said. Arsenal’s title tilt last season was ended by six draws and they will have to improve on that if they are to challenge this season.Sophie DowneyWSL roundup: Arsenal rue misses in Palace drawView image in fullscreenChloe Kelly and Leah Williamson were part of a dominant, but goalless, Arsenal display against Crystal Palace.Photograph: Eddie Keogh/WSL/Getty ImagesWest Ham expose London CityAfterbeating Manchester Unitedlast time out, London City Lionesses were brought back down to earth by an inspired West Ham to suffer their first defeat of the campaign. West Ham put in a performance that caught the eye for their own qualities as well as highlighting the early frailties of Eder Maestre’s team. If you were to just glance at the stats, you would think the visitors dominated, but it felt anything like that at Dagenham: Rita Guarino, the Hammers manager, set up her team perfectly. The burgeoning midfield relationship between Katie Zelem and Saki Kumagai nullified the threat of Alexia Putellas and Rosa Kafaji, Riko Ueki swept everything up in front of them, while the combined transitional threat of Viviane Asseyi and Kelly Gago had London City’s right side teetering. West Ham’s French duo found their touch in front of goal after precise counterattacking moves to secure a first win of the new season.SDMatch report: West Ham 2-1 London City LionessesFlexibility helps Liverpool close the gapTwo games, four points and frustration that it is not all six: Liverpool have come a long way in a year. Last season, it took them until 25 January to earn a win and that win came against their opponents on Sunday, Tottenham, a similarly resurgent side who are possibly a few steps further ahead in their project. It was tactical flexibility that helped Gareth Taylor’s side earn a draw, with Liverpool responding well after Signe Gaupset’s effort took a heavy deflection off Sam Kerr to give Spurs a lead, somewhat against the run of play. The half-time introduction of Aurélie Csillag, who joined in January and grabbed the goal that gave them a point, was key. “They’re not going to give up the spaces easily,” said Taylor. “At times the spaces changed. Aurélie coming on to the pitch is a different type of proposition for back-fours as she’s physically very good.”SWChampions flex their muscleThe only team with a perfect record after two games, Manchester City, the reigning WSL champions, showed they can be ruthless, with a comprehensive 4-1 defeat of Aston Villa. Yes, City have played a promoted side, Birmingham, and an unconvincing Aston Villa. Yes, we are yet to see how City fare when they add Champions League football into the mix, but the firepower at Andrée Jeglertz’s disposal is enviable. Khadija Shaw has three goals from two games and City had 55 touches in the opposition area to Villa’s 15 and 23 shots to Villa’s five. Chelsea’s profligacy cost them last weekend and Arsenal’s cost them this weekend, but City are scoring for fun.SWskip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toMoving the GoalpostsNo topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionView image in fullscreenManchester City’s Khadija Shaw scored her third goal of the season at Aston Villa.Photograph: Andrew Couldridge/Action Images/ReutersHills’ regret after red cardThe Charlton manager, Karen Hills, said she was disappointed after the second-half red card for Ashleigh Neville against Everton led to a 1-0 defeat. Neville was sent off in the 58th minute for a high boot on Ruby Mace. While Hills suggested there was more hip-to-hip contact than anything else, she did not outright criticise the officials. “I don’t think the referee made the decision, it’s the fourth [official] and I guess they have to work together. Yes, her foot is a little bit high, but disappointed because that changes the game.” Charlton went down to nine players after Hawa Cissoko received two yellow cards in quick succession.Emillia HawkinsView image in fullscreenAshleigh Neville was sent off in the 58th minute for a high challenge.Photograph: Molly Darlington/WSL/Getty ImagesBirmingham’s lack of WSL experience showsOn paper, Birmingham’s 2-2 draw against Brighton is an impressive feat for a promoted side, but the head coach, Amy Merricks, did not look too happy at the final whistle. Her team led the match by two goals with 15 minutes left to play, but Olivia Garcia got one back for Brighton in the 77th minute before Kiko Seike snatched a point with a last-gasp equaliser. The difference in experience between the two sides probably played a part in the later stages, with Birmingham in the WSL for the first time since 2022. “We’ll take a massive lesson today from those dying moments and how we see that out a bit better,” said Merricks. “What we can’t question is this group’s application and intent. They were on the front foot, they were tenacious. We look improved from last week, which, for me, is brilliant. We’re going to go up a notch because I know this team, they won’t settle, they’re very hungry.”EHPosTeamPGDPts1Man City Women2562Chelsea Women2543Liverpool FC Women2444Tottenham Hotspur Women2245Arsenal Women2146Crystal Palace Women2147London City Lionesses2038Everton Women2039West Ham Women2-1310Brighton & Hove Albion Women2-1111Birmingham City Women2-2112Aston Villa Women2-3113Charlton Women2-5014Man Utd Women2-60Explore more on these topicsWomen's Super LeagueWomen's footballManchester United WomenChelsea WomenArsenal WomenCrystal Palace WomenWest Ham United WomenfeaturesShareReuse this content
